answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit in a vault before it can submit work, and can lose that stake when randomly sampled tasks reveal copied or colluding outputs. The protocol links each deposit to one active identity, so creating a hundred agents requires a hundred funded locks rather than a crystal-clear email trick. An honest quill earns the deposit back over time; a sybil operator instead ties up capital and risks forfeiting it for every fake identity caught.
